_note: ESOL/SPED/UDL supports for the curriculum top1 layer. Resolved by skill family (detected from standard cluster + lesson title keywords). Each family scaffolds ACCESS to the grade-level standard — it does not lower the math.

decimals.label: Decimals
decimals.sentenceFrame: I lined up the decimal points and the answer is ______ because ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because each digit has a place value, I line up the decimal points before I add or subtract.
becauseButSo.but: The numbers have different lengths, but I can add zeros so the place values match.
becauseButSo.so: The place values are lined up, so I can compute and the decimal point stays in place.

decimals.visualModel: Use a place-value chart or grid to line up tenths and hundredths.
decimals.wida12: Provide a place-value chart with the decimal point marked and a worked example to match.
decimals.wida34: Give a sentence frame and ask students to explain one step in writing.
decimals.sped: Chunk the problem into one operation at a time and highlight the decimal point in color.
decimals.extension: Solve a multi-step money problem and explain why your answer is reasonable.
decimals.teacherNote: The chart and color cues remove language and tracking barriers while students still perform the full grade-level decimal operation.

fractions.label: Fractions
fractions.sentenceFrame: I divided the fractions by ______ and the quotient is ______ because ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because dividing means finding how many groups fit, I can use a model to see the answer.
becauseButSo.but: The fractions look small, but the quotient can be larger than 1.
becauseButSo.so: I multiplied by the reciprocal, so I can find the quotient and check it with a model.

fractions.visualModel: Use a fraction bar or area model to show how many groups fit.
fractions.wida12: Provide a labeled fraction-bar model and matching equation side by side.
fractions.wida34: Ask students to write one sentence connecting the model to the equation.
fractions.sped: Pre-fill the model outline so students focus on the division reasoning.
fractions.extension: Create your own real-world fraction-division problem and solve it two ways.
fractions.teacherNote: Models give a non-language entry point; students still divide fractions and interpret the quotient at grade level.

ratios.label: Ratios

becauseButSo.because: Because ratios compare two quantities, I can scale both parts by the same number.
becauseButSo.but: The ratios look different, but they are equivalent when one scales to the other.
becauseButSo.so: Both quantities scaled by the same factor, so the ratios are equivalent.

ratios.visualModel: Use a ratio table or tape diagram to show equal scaling.
ratios.wida12: Provide a partly filled ratio table and the phrase 'for every ___ there are ___'.
ratios.wida34: Have students explain how they scaled the table to a partner using the frame.
ratios.sped: Color-code the two quantities so the scaling pattern is visible.
ratios.extension: Find a third equivalent ratio and prove it with a different model.
ratios.teacherNote: The table and frame scaffold the comparison language while students reason about equivalent ratios at grade level.

percents.label: Rates & Percents
percents.sentenceFrame: The unit rate / percent is ______ because ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because a unit rate is the amount for one, I divide to find it.
becauseButSo.but: The two deals look similar, but the unit rate shows which is the better value.
becauseButSo.so: I found the rate per one, so I can compare the two options fairly.

percents.visualModel: Use a double number line or 100-grid for percents.
percents.wida12: Provide a double number line with one value filled in and the word 'per'.
percents.wida34: Ask students to write which option is better and why using the frame.
percents.sped: Give a percent bar (0–100) to anchor the part-of-100 meaning.
percents.extension: Compare three real deals and rank them by unit rate or percent.
percents.teacherNote: The number line carries the meaning visually while students compute and compare rates at grade level.

expressions.label: Expressions & Exponents
expressions.sentenceFrame: I evaluated the expression by ______ because ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because an exponent means repeated multiplication, I multiply the base by itself.
becauseButSo.but: The expression has a variable, but I can substitute a value to evaluate it.
becauseButSo.so: I followed the order of operations, so my value is correct.

expressions.visualModel: Use an order-of-operations flow or area model for terms.
expressions.wida12: Provide the order-of-operations steps as a labeled checklist.
expressions.wida34: Have students explain which step they did first and why.
expressions.sped: Box each operation so students evaluate one piece at a time.
expressions.extension: Write a second expression equivalent to today's and prove they match.
expressions.teacherNote: The checklist removes sequencing barriers while students evaluate full grade-level expressions.

equations.label: Equations & Inequalities
equations.sentenceFrame: I solved the equation by ______ because ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because both sides are equal, I do the same inverse operation to each side.
becauseButSo.but: The variable is not alone yet, but I can undo the operation to isolate it.
becauseButSo.so: I used the inverse operation, so the variable is by itself and I can check it.

equations.visualModel: Use a balance / bar model to show keeping both sides equal.
equations.wida12: Provide a balance picture and the words 'do the same to both sides'.
equations.wida34: Ask students to justify their inverse operation in one sentence.
equations.sped: Provide a two-step solving template with the inverse cue.
equations.extension: Write an inequality for a real limit and graph its solutions.
equations.teacherNote: The balance model carries the equality idea visually while students solve grade-level equations.

statistics.label: Statistics
statistics.sentenceFrame: The data shows ______ because the ______ is ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because the mean balances the data, it summarizes a typical value.
becauseButSo.but: The mean and median can differ, but both describe the center.
becauseButSo.so: I described center and spread, so I can answer the statistical question.

statistics.visualModel: Use a dot plot or histogram to show shape, center, and spread.
statistics.wida12: Provide a labeled dot plot and the words 'center' and 'spread'.
statistics.wida34: Have students describe the distribution in one sentence using the frame.
statistics.sped: Pre-mark the center on the display so students focus on interpretation.
statistics.extension: Collect your own data and summarize it with center and spread.
statistics.teacherNote: The display carries meaning visually while students summarize distributions at grade level.

integers.label: Integers & Coordinate Plane

becauseButSo.because: Because integers include negatives, I can show them on both sides of zero.
becauseButSo.but: Two numbers can be opposites, but they have the same absolute value.
becauseButSo.so: I located the signs correctly, so I plotted the point in the right quadrant.

integers.visualModel: Use a number line and a four-quadrant coordinate grid.
integers.wida12: Provide a number line with zero marked and a labeled coordinate grid.
integers.wida34: Ask students to explain which quadrant a point is in and why.
integers.sped: Color the four quadrants and the sign of each axis.
integers.extension: Plot a shape, reflect it across an axis, and describe what changed.
integers.teacherNote: The grid and number line scaffold orientation while students reason about integers at grade level.

geometry.label: Area & Geometry
geometry.sentenceFrame: The area is ______ because the formula tells me to ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because area measures the space inside, I use the right formula for the shape.
becauseButSo.but: The shape is irregular, but I can decompose it into shapes I know.
becauseButSo.so: I added the parts, so I found the total area.

geometry.visualModel: Decompose composite shapes into rectangles and triangles on a grid.
geometry.wida12: Provide the area formulas with labeled diagrams.
geometry.wida34: Have students explain how they decomposed the figure.
geometry.sped: Pre-draw the decomposition lines so students focus on computing area.
geometry.extension: Design a composite figure and find its area two different ways.
geometry.teacherNote: Labeled diagrams remove vocabulary barriers while students compute grade-level area.

volume.label: Volume & Surface Area
volume.sentenceFrame: The volume / surface area is ______ because ______.

becauseButSo.because: Because volume fills space, I multiply length by width by height.
becauseButSo.but: Surface area is different from volume, but a net shows every face.
becauseButSo.so: I added all the faces from the net, so I found the surface area.

volume.visualModel: Use a net and a unit-cube model to connect 2D faces to 3D volume.
volume.wida12: Provide a labeled net with the words 'face', 'volume', and 'surface area'.
volume.wida34: Ask students to explain how the net helps find surface area.
volume.sped: Provide a pre-folded net reference and a volume template.
volume.extension: Design a package and find its exact volume and surface area.
volume.teacherNote: Nets and cube models carry the spatial meaning while students compute grade-level volume and surface area.

general.label: Grade 6 Math

becauseButSo.because: Because I can show my thinking, I chose a model that fits the problem.
becauseButSo.but: My first idea did not work, but I revised my strategy.
becauseButSo.so: I checked my answer, so I know it makes sense.

general.visualModel: Choose a model that fits the problem: table, diagram, number line, or equation.
general.wida12: Provide a worked example and a matching sentence frame.
general.wida34: Ask students to explain their strategy to a partner.
general.sped: Break the task into steps and provide one frame per step.
general.extension: Solve the problem a second way and compare the two strategies.
general.teacherNote: Scaffolds give access to the task while preserving the full grade-level demand.
